title: Container-based framework for large-scale spiking network simulation
summary: This study presents a containerization framework using Singularity/Apptainer to enable portable and reproducible simulations of large-scale spiking neural networks on heterogeneous high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructures. The authors encapsulated the CoreNEURON simulation engine, compilers, MPI libraries, and GPU toolchains within a single image. Benchmarking against a replicated cerebellar granular layer model containing approximately 1 million neurons demonstrated that containerization introduced negligible performance overhead (~0.2% to ~1%) compared to native installations while ensuring bit-identical results across different CPU architectures (Intel Xeon Silver vs. Intel Core i7) and GPU generations (Tesla V100-SXM2, Quadro GP100, TITAN Xp). The framework facilitates the deployment of complex computational neuroscience workflows without requiring host system modifications.
tldr: A container-based Singularity/Apptainer framework enables portable, reproducible large-scale spiking neural network simulations with negligible performance overhead across heterogeneous HPC systems using CoreNEURON and GPU acceleration.
evidence: This study introduces a framework utilizing containerization technology to ensure scalable and reproducible simulations by encapsulating the entire software stack... within a portable image.

Our results demonstrate that containerized simulations introduce little performance penalty compared to native installations while delivering identical results across multiple systems with minimal effort, providing a robust solution for portability.
